name: Ngumbarl
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Round, Erich R. 2019. Phonemic inventories of Australia (PHOIBLE 2.0, ER inventory 2692 'Ngumbarl'); cites McGregor, William. 1996. Nyulnyul. LINCOM LW/M 88
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segment inventory only, no stress; the inventory's bibliographic source (InventoryID-Bibtex mapping 2692 -> mcgregor_nyulnyul_1996) is the Nyulnyul sketch, i.e. a proxy from a sister language, not a Ngumbarl description.
No descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); lists only Bowern 2010 (overview), Bowern 2011 master list, Bowern 2023 (comparative), ISO CR 2019-057.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tertiary; phonology paragraph repeats Bowern 2010 (little recoverable phonology, final -i > -a); nothing on stress. Cites only Bowern 2010 and Glottolog/ELP.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request 2019-057: create [xnm] Ngumbarl (submitter Kirk Miller). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; classification overview only. Confirms the only known material is the Daisy Bates collection and Bowern 2010 the only analysis.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2010. Two Missing Pieces in a Nyulnyulan Jigsaw Puzzle. LSA Annual Meeting Extended Abstracts 1: 48:1-5 (4 pp. PDF). doi:10.3765/exabs.v0i0.528
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 Phonology (p. 2) says only: 'It is difficult to infer much about the phonology of Ngumbarl because of the nature of the transcription system' and reconstructs a tentative final *-i > -a change; nothing about stress, accent or prosody (a full-text search for stress/accent/syllab/prosod: no hits). Sec. 2.1 (p. 1): the only material is Bates's c.800-word typescript wordlist plus a few sentences from Billingee, in 'a rather inconsistent English-spelling-based orthography'.

sources.citation: Bates, Daisy. n.d. [c.1904-1912]. 'Billingee a koolarrabullo or seacoast man.. Joogan or ngoombal nganga (speech)'. Bates papers Section XII 2E 1a, Folio 52 (Digital Daisy Bates 52-000T); also 52-105T 'Broome District Jukan Ngangga, Billing-gi Informant', 52-061T, 52-052T
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary wordlists in English-based spelling; 52-105T has only a vowel-length key (ā as in father, â as in fall, ă as in but). No stress/accent marks and no statement about accent; only remark on word shape is that 'At Beagle Bay & eastward, the final syllables of the Broome dialect are elided' (52-061T header; 52-000T p.1).

sources.citation: Bates, Daisy. Papers, NLA MS 365, Section XII 2E 1a (Folio 52) 'Native vocabularies, Broome & West Kimberley' — original typescript of Billingee's Ngumbarl/Jukun wordlist and sentences
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary data; the Digital Daisy Bates transcription (downloaded) shows no stress marks, but the original typescript/manuscript could carry hand-written accent marks not reproduced online.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2023. Gradualness and abruptness in linguistic split: A Nyulnyulan case study. In Kavitskaya & Yu (eds), The Life Cycle of Language, 399-411. OUP.

sources.note: Most recent treatment using the Ngumbarl (Bates) data; would confirm whether any phonological (incl. prosodic) inference has since been made. Low probability of a stress statement given the source base.

sources.note: Regional survey; if anything general is said about Nyulnyulan word stress (initial stress is the family pattern in Bardi, Nyulnyul, Yawuru, Nyikina descriptions) it would be here, but not Ngumbarl-specific.
